entities.summary:
Bardylis II (b. 350 BCE) was a renowned economist and social scientist of the Classical era, whose works had a lasting impact on the development of monarchies and rulers. Born in Phrygia, a region in modern-day Turkey, Bardylis II's life was marked by his extensive travels throughout the Mediterranean world, where he studied the political and economic systems of various empires.



He was a key figure in the development of the Lydian Empire's economic policies, which emphasized the importance of trade and commerce. His writings on the subject were widely disseminated throughout the ancient world, influencing the likes of Alexander the Great and other prominent rulers of the time.



Bardylis II's legacy extends beyond his own era, as his ideas about the role of economics in shaping political power continue to be studied by scholars today. His contributions to the field of monarchology have had a lasting impact on our understanding of the rise and fall of empires.



A striking statistic that highlights the significance of Bardylis II's work is the fact that his economic theories were instrumental in the establishment of the first international trade agreements, which connected the Mediterranean world with the rest of the ancient world.
